\section*{Question 4}

Consider the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y^{2}}{x-1}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] On the axes provided, sketch a slope field for the given differential equation at the six points indicated.
\item[(b)] Let \(y=f(x)\) be the particular solution to the given differential equation with the initial condition \(f(2)=3\). Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(y=f(x)\) at \(x=2\). Use your equation to approximate \(f(2.1)\).
\item[(c)] Find the particular solution \(y=f(x)\) to the given differential equation with the initial condition \(f(2)=3\).
\item[(a)]
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/5c5fe09e-fe6f-4f19-86f7-7e1750e3f6f8-1.jpg?height=520&width=385&top_left_y=885&top_left_x=249)
\item[(b)] \(\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(x, y)=(2,3)}=\frac{3^{2}}{2-1}=9\)
An equation for the tangent line is \(y=9(x-2)+3\).
\[
f(2.1) \approx 9(2.1-2)+3=3.9
\]
\item[(c)] \(\frac{1}{y^{2}} d y=\frac{1}{x-1} d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{1}{y^{2}} d y=\int \frac{1}{x-1} d x \\
& -\frac{1}{y}=\ln |x-1|+C \\
& -\frac{1}{3}=\ln |2-1|+C \Rightarrow C=-\frac{1}{3} \\
& -\frac{1}{y}=\ln |x-1|-\frac{1}{3} \\
& y=\frac{1}{\frac{1}{3}-\ln (x-1)}
\end{aligned}
\]
Note: This solution is valid for \(1<x<1+e^{1 / 3}\).
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { zero slopes } \\ 1: \text { nonzero slopes }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { tangent line equation } \\ 1: \text { approximation }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(5:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { separation of variables } \\ 2: \text { antiderivatives } \\ 1: \text { constant of integration and } \\ \quad \text { uses initial condition } \\ 1: \text { solves for } y\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] Note: \(\max 3 / 5\) [1-2-0-0] if no constant of integration
\item[] Note: 0/5 if no separation of variables
\end{itemize}
